newsitem.title: INDIA: Two airliners collide over India, 350 feared dead.
newsitem.headline: Two airliners collide over India, 350 feared dead.

text.p: Around 350 people were feared dead on Tuesday when a Saudi Arabian jumbo jet and a Kazakhstan airliner collided in mid-air west of New Delhi, aviation officials told Reuters.
If the toll is confirmed, the air disaster will be among the world's five worst for loss of life and the worst involving two aircraft in flight.
The officials said there were 312 people, including 23 crew, aboard the Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp Boeing 747 and 39, including 10 crew, aboard the other aircraft, a Tupolev TU-154.
"There is hardly any chance of survivors," one official said.
Ranjan Chatterjee, chairman of the Airports Authority of India, told a news conference: "We have not heard of any survivors so far. It seems rather difficult, unfortunately."
The Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency said three survivors were pulled from the wreckage but that they died on the way to hospital.
The collision occurred as night was falling over India.
Officials said wreckage had been sighted at villages in Haryana State, bordering New Delhi.
"They collided between 6.40 p.m. (1310 GMT) and 6.41 p.m. (1311 GMT) Indian Standard Time," airport operations official Robey Lal told Reuters at New Delhi airport.
Officials of the directorate general of civil aviation said the Saudi airliner had been cleared to climb to a flight level of 14,000 feet (4,270 metres) by air traffic control in New Delhi.
They said the Kazakh airliner had been cleared to descend to 15,000 feet (4,570 metres).
"Radar blips of both aircraft disappeared at 1840 hrs (1310 GMT), 40 nautical miles southwest of Delhi," one official said.
One aviation source described the aftermath of the collision as "like a bolt of lightning.
"Two streaks of fire descended down to the ground," he said.
Another eyewitness, quoted by the PTI said: "I saw a ball of flame hurtling down and I could make out that it was an aircraft."
The agency said the collision occurred over Jhajhar in the Rohtak district of Haryana, about 80 km (50 miles) from New Delhi.
The Indian government has ordered an inquiry into the collision, aviation officials said.
Officials said the Saudi plane, with a flight number of SV 763, had been bound for Dhahran and Jeddah in Saudi Arabia.
They said the Kazakh plane, with flight number KZA 1407, was had been travelling from Chimkent in Kazakhstan to New Delhi.
This was the third disaster involving a TU-154 in the past year. The aircraft are the workhorses of airlines in the former Soviet Union.
Indian civil aviation officials said the Tupolev had been chartered but gave no details.
The previous worst mid-air accident was when a British Trident and a Yugoslav DC9 collided over Zagreb in 1976 with the loss of 176 lives.
